lines: In rising markets, dated futures usually trade above spot
scenes.sub: In rising markets, dated futures usually trade above spot. The gap (basis) shrinks to zero at expiry because the future settles at spot. Buy spot + short the future at the same size and you lock that gap, whatever the price does, as long as
scenes.vo: In rising markets, dated futures usually trade above spot. The gap (basis) shrinks to zero at expiry because the future settles at spot. Buy spot + short the future at the same size and you lock that gap, whatever the price does, as long as both legs survive to expiry. annualised basis = (future divided by spot minus 1) times 365 divided by days
scenes.cap: In rising markets, dated futures usually trade above spot. The gap (basis) shrinks to zero at expiry because the future settles at spot. Buy spot + short the future at the same size and you lock that gap, whatever the price does, as long as both legs survive to expiry. annualised basis = (future ÷ spot − 1) × 365 ÷ days

scenes.title: Worked example: ETH spot 3,000, 90-day future 3,060
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. ETH spot 3,000, 90-day future 3,060. minus 1,440 per ETH. Without enough margin on the futures venue, it's closed out and you're left long spot at the top. At expiry, if ETH is 2,000: spot leg minus 1,000, short future +1,060 to +60 per ETH. At expiry, if ETH is 4,500: spot leg +1,500, short future minus 1,440 to +60 per ETH. The catch: before expiry, a rally to 4,500 means the short leg shows. You can check every number with the program's calculator.

scenes.sub: Margin and venue risk: a squeeze on the short leg, or the venue failing.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Both legs opened together, same size
Futures margin survives at least a +100% move, or a rule to top up
Plan to hold to expiry; early exit may be at a worse basis
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, Both legs opened together, same size. Next, Futures margin survives at least a +100% move, or a rule to top up. Then, Venue risk sized (cap per venue). And finally, Plan to hold to expiry; early exit may be at a worse basis.

scenes.vo: Question one. Spot 2,000, 180-day future 2,080. Annualised basis? [[pause 4]] The answer: 4% times 365 to 180 about 8.1%.
scenes.cap: Question 1. Spot 2,000, 180-day future 2,080. Annualised basis? The answer: 4% × 365/180 ≈ 8.1%.

scenes.q: Why is the return "locked" at expiry?
scenes.a: The future settles at spot, so the gain on one leg offsets the loss on the other, leaving the entry basis.

scenes.q: What breaks the trade before expiry?
scenes.a: A margin call or liquidation on the short future during a rally, or venue failure.
